text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S Secretary of State Madeleine Albright made a strong plea for maintaining normal trade relations with China in the face of stepped-up congressional efforts to revoke Beijing's Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) privileges.

- In an unprecedented move, the Chief Justice cut the jail sentence of a Burmese man from two years to about three months after finding he had been convicted wrongly under a harsher provision of the criminal law.
- Wing Tai Holdings stunned the market yesterday with its bid for a choice condominium site in Draycott Park -- the highest price yet for 99-year leasehold land in Singapore.
- Thailand's moves to stop foreign stock investors repatriating the baht could dampen sentiment on the already plunging bourse, brokers and analysts said.

- State-controlled China Everbright, currently making waves in Hong Kong with numerous asset acquisitions, has set up a regional headquarters in Singapore as part of a move to expand into Southeast Asia.
- The Straits Times Industrials Index dropped below the 2,000 level for the second time this year, finishing within a hair's breadth of its year's low.
- The US dollar tumbled to a seven-month low against the yen on news that Japan's current account surplus leapt by nearly 93 percent to 1.09 trillion yen in April.

- Tycoon Ting Pek Khiing's M$15.5 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam project suffered a double blow with news that damage to a temporary structure could delay construction and that response to a rights issue to part-finance the project has been lukewarm.
- Dr Judy Lim, the outgoing chief executive of Tan Tock Seng Hospital, will join RSP Architects Planners & Engineers as its CEO from July 1.
- Hotel Properties Ltd's Singapore $117 million carrying value for its Four Seasons Hotel project in Milan is contingent on HPL's continued financial support, its auditors said.

- Disappointed investors dumped their Cerebos shares, clipping about Singapore $380 million off the value of the food-based company and dragging the market index below lthe 2,000-point level in the process.
- Phone-cord maker Huan Hsin Holdings chalked up a moderate premium of 10.7 percent on its mainboard debut, closing 4.5 US cents above its offer price at 46.5 US cents.

- Former Amcol Holdings executive directors Ng Chee Kheong and Llyod Lochra paid accused businessman Peter Tay a commission for his role in a Mauritian joint venture to prevent him complaining to other Amcol board members about their conduct, it was claimed in court.
- Inno-Pacific Holdings (Inno-Pac) is selling yet another company -- its ailing poultry processing farm -- in its continuing struggle to staunch the group's losses.
